These parameters varied for each volunteer and for cach class configuration, aimed at obtaining the best classification accuracies. Englehart et al. (1999) and other researchers such as Basu, Battacharyya and Kin (2010) and Zhang (2000) defend that MIP, as long as properly trained and with an appropriate configuration will always match, if not exceed, the performance of an RIDA. But usually, due to the need to automate MLP training over a large number of interactions, the number of hidden layers and also the number of neurons are fixed. For a given subject and a specific number of classes however, the configuration may be inappropriate, and will be inhibit the generalization performance of the MLP.

The RLDA, on the other hand does not require these specifications, and performs very well.
